description: Fetch a web page through UnblockingAPI's rotating residential proxies and a real browser. Useful for pages a plain HTTP fetch can't read: pages that need JavaScript, refuse automated requests, or show different content by country. Returns the page as Markdown (or cleaned HTML with format: 'html'); select narrows it to the part you need. If content is missing, fetch again with scroll_steps or wait_for. Picks the mode itself by default: a plain HTTP fetch first, and a real browser when the site blocks it or needs JavaScript. Pass a template reference to get structured JSON instead of HTML — call find_templates with the url first to see whether one exists. Costs 1 credit per successful fetch; failures are free.

detect_ms.description: Implies a browser. How long to probe wait_rules guards before falling back to wait_for. Default 800.

format.description: How the page comes back (template results are always JSON). "markdown" (default): text, headings, links and lists, a fraction of the size. "html": the cleaned markup, for attributes, custom elements and choosing a select.

fresh.description: Fetch again even if this exact fetch was made in the last 10 minutes (by default that copy is reused for free).

location.description: 2-letter country code to proxy through (e.g. 'us', 'gb', 'de'). Most countries are supported; an unsupported one is refused with the list.

max_age.description: Accept a cached copy of the same request up to this many seconds old (0–300). Cache hits return in milliseconds and still cost 1 credit. Default 0 = always fetch fresh.

max_chars.description: Cap on returned body characters (default 80000, max 140000). Longer bodies are cut with a note; select narrows a page to the part you need instead.

render.description: Omit to let the API decide (plain fetch first, a browser when blocked or when the page is an empty JavaScript shell; learned per site). true always renders with a real browser (slower, up to ~2 min worst case); false never does. Any wait option implies true.

scroll_steps.description: Implies a browser. Scroll down this many times before the readiness check, to trigger lazy-loaded sections. Bounded discovery, not a way to collect an infinite list.

select.description: CSS selector: return only the matching elements (e.g. 'article', 'table tr', 'shreddit-post'), in the chosen format. Re-reading a fetch with another select or format reuses the page already fetched - no credit.

settle_ms.description: Implies a browser. Ceiling (not a delay) on the settle wait, default 5000. Capture happens as soon as the DOM has been quiet for 500ms. Use wait_min_ms for a minimum delay; lower this to cap the worst case.

template.description: Parse the page with a published template and return JSON instead of HTML. Takes a template reference like 'handle/name' — call find_templates with this url first to see whether one covers the site. Append '@<version>' to pin a version (the response's template_version is the one that answered). The template forces its own render and wait settings.

url.description: The HTTP/HTTPS URL to fetch. Media and binary files are rejected.

wait_for.description: Implies a browser. When to capture: 'stable' (default — once the DOM stops changing), 'domcontentloaded' (immediately), 'networkidle', or any CSS selector (wait until it is visible, then settle). Prefer a selector or 'stable' on pages that never go quiet.

wait_min_ms.description: Implies a browser. Minimum delay after navigation before scrolling or checking readiness, for content that is absent from the first capture.

wait_rules.description: Implies a browser. Conditional waits for pages with several possible layouts (consent gate, interstitial, A/B variant). Each 'if' selector is probed in order for detect_ms; the first visible one wins and its 'then' replaces wait_for. Example: [{if: '#consent', then: '#results'}].

if.description: CSS selector to probe for visibility.

then.description: Replacement wait_for when the guard is visible: a mode or a CSS selector. Empty = capture as-is.

wait_state.description: Condition for a CSS selector in wait_for (requires one): 'visible' (default), 'nonempty' (visible text, ignoring loading placeholders), 'hidden' (all matches hidden or gone — e.g. a spinner), 'stable' (text and match count unchanged for 750ms).
